Rashi on Chullin 31a:10:1.hebrew: מחטא דאושכפי - מרצע הרצענין, שפיותיו חדודין וחותכין חוטי התפר:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:10:1.english: A needle of the cobblers - The awl of the cobblers, whose edges are sharp and cut the threads of the stitching.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:13:1.hebrew: ואע"ג דלא מיכוין - לשחוט אלא להפלת סכין, מאן תנא:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:13:1.english: And even though he did not intend - to slaughter, but only to make the knife fall, who taught [this mishna]?

Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:1.hebrew: זעירא דמן חבריא - צעיר הישיבה. ולי נראה דאושעיא זעירא היה נקרא דמן חבריא, שמבני הישיבה:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:1.english: Ze'ira of the fellows - The youngest of the yeshiva. And it seems to me that Oshaya Ze'ira was called "of the fellows" because he was among the members of the yeshiva.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:2.hebrew: הוא תני לה - שונה המשנה מרבו:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:2.english: He taught it - He learns the mishna from his teacher.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:3.hebrew: והוא אמר - מדעתו שהלכה כרבי נתן:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:14:3.english: And he said - On his own reasoning, that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Natan.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:15:1.hebrew: והא אמרה רבא חדא זימנא - ולמה ליה לרבא למידק ממתניתין, ולמימר "הא הפילה הוא כשרה", ולאשמועינן דסתם לן תנא כר' נתן? הא אשמועינן רבא חדא זימנא דסתם לן תנא כרבי נתן:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:15:1.english: But Rava already said this once - Why did Rava need to infer from the mishna, and say, "But if he [himself] dropped it, it is valid," and to teach us that the Tanna taught an unattributed [ruling] for us in accordance with R. Natan? Rava already taught us once that the Tanna taught an unattributed [ruling] for us in accordance with R. Natan.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:15:2.english: And all of them who slaughtered - A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:16:1.english: It is necessary - for Rava to teach us both [rulings].

Rashi on Chullin 31a:16:2.hebrew: אבל הכא דלא מיכוין - אפילו לחתיכה בעלמא. אי לאו דאשמועינן רבא, לא הוה דייקנא מיניה "הא הפילה הוא כשרה", דאפילו הפילה הוא הוה אמינא דפסולה, והיא גופה איצטריכא לאשמועינן "מה שאתה זובח אתה אוכל", דבעינן שחיטה מכח אדם. קמ"ל רבא דהא נמי דייקנא מינה, מדלא קתני "הפיל סכין" או "זרק סכין". והא דפריך "והא אמרה רבא חדא זימנא", ולא פריך "תנינא חדא זימנא", משום דבמתניתין לא תני בהדיא "הפילה הוא" דכשרה, אלא רבא דייק לה:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:16:2.english: But here, where he did not intend - Even for merely cutting something. Had Rava not taught us [this], we would not have inferred from it [the mishna] that if he himself dropped it, it is valid, for I would have thought that even if he himself dropped it, it is invalid. And that itself [the mishna's ruling] needed to teach us [the principle] "what you slaughter, you eat", [meaning] that we require slaughter to be performed by human force. Rava therefore teaches us that we also infer this from it, since [the mishna] does not state "he dropped the knife" or "he threw the knife." And as for the fact that [the Gemara] asks, "But Rava already said this once," and does not ask, "We already learned this once [in a mishna]," [this is] because the mishna does not state explicitly that if he himself dropped it, it is valid; rather, Rava infers it.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:18:1.hebrew: נדה שנאנסה וטבלה - לקמיה מפרש היכי נאנסה:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:18:1.english: A menstruant woman who was forced and immersed - Below [the Gemara] explains how she was forced.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:18:2.english: To her home - To be permitted to her husband:

Rashi on Chullin 31a:19:1.hebrew: טמא שאכל תרומה - במיתה בידי שמים, באלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף פג.). וכרת חמור ממיתה, דימיו נכרתים וזרעו נכרת, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ) ערירים יהיו:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:19:1.english: An impure person who ate terumah - [is liable to] death at the hands of Heaven, in [the chapter] "These are the ones who are burned" (Sanhedrin 83a). And karet is more severe than death, for his days are cut off and his offspring are cut off, as it is written (Leviticus 20): "They shall be childless."

Rashi on Chullin 31a:1:1.english: Gidfei - The feathers that surround the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:1:2.hebrew: דמיפרמי - כרותות, מינצייר"ש בלע"ז, דאי עבד חלדה מבפנים, היה יוצא רוחב פי החץ בין הכנפים ולא היה חותכו:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:1:2.english: That are split [demiframi] - Cut off, [called] *mincier* in Old French [i.e., cut up, sliced]. For if the mole had made [the hole] from the inside, the width of the arrow's mouth would have protruded between the wings, and it would not have cut it.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:20:1.hebrew: ומנא תימרא - דלחולין לא בעינן כוונה:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:20:1.english: And from where do you say - That for non-sacred food [ḥullin] we do not require intent?

Rashi on Chullin 31a:20:2.english: That was detached - from the sea.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:20:3.hebrew: ה"ג מה כלים דלא מיכווני - דהא לית להו דעת:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:20:3.english: This is the correct version: "Just as utensils, which are not directed [by intent]" - For they have no awareness.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:2:1.hebrew: צריך שיתן עפר - תיחוח למטה, דאם העפר קשה לא מקרי עפר למטה:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:2:1.english: He must put down earth - Loose earth underneath, for if the earth is hard, it is not called "earth" underneath.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:2:2.english: In earth - This implies that all of it is buried in earth.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:3:1.hebrew: דמזמין ליה לעפרא דכולה פתקא - עפר כל הבקעה היה מסיע וכותש, או שהיה עפר תיחוח ומזמנו [בפה] לכך:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:3:1.english: That he designates for him the dirt of the entire plain - [The slaughterer] would move and crush the dirt of the entire plain, or it was loose dirt, and he designated it [orally] for this purpose.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:4:1.hebrew: א"ר זירא מלא צואר - דמתניתין חוץ לצואר בעינן, ולא תימא מלא צואר דוקא:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:4:1.english: Rabbi Zeira said: the full width of the neck - For [the case in] our mishna, we require [that the knife go] outside the neck; but do not say that the full width of the neck [is required] specifically.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:5:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו - האי "חוץ לצואר" דרבי זירא, משהו קאמר, או מלא צואר קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:5:1.english: A question was raised before them - This "outside the neck" of Rabbi Zeira: does he mean any amount, or does he mean the full width of the neck?

Rashi on Chullin 31a:6:1.hebrew: אלא פשיטא מלא צואר חוץ לשני צוארים וש"מ מלא צואר - דקתני מתניתין נמי ברישא, אחוץ לצואר קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:6:1.english: Rather, it is obvious: [the case is] a full neck's width outside the two necks, and one may learn from this [the law of] a full neck's width - For the mishna also taught in its first clause [that] it refers to [a cut] outside the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:8:1.hebrew: שאין לו קרנים - דרגילין היו לעשות כמין קרנים לאזמילין לנוי, על גביהן מטין לצד ראשן, ומתוך שהוא קטן מאד הוא נשמט מן הצואר, וכשהוא מוליך ומביא יש לחוש שמא יחלידו הסימנין או ינקבו אותן הקרני':
Rashi on Chullin 31a:8:1.english: That it has no horns - For it was customary to make a sort of horns on scalpels, for decoration, on top of them, bent toward their tip. And since [the scalpel] is very small, it slips out of the neck, and when he moves it forward and back, there is reason to worry lest the windpipe and gullet be burrowed into [under the flesh, ḥaldah], or lest those horns puncture them.

Rashi on Chullin 31a:9:1.hebrew: מיבזע בזע - כשמוליך ומביא, מתוך שהוא חד הוא נוקב וקורע ולא חותך:
Rashi on Chullin 31a:9:1.english: It tears, it tears - When he moves [the knife] back and forth, since it is sharp, it pierces and tears and does not cut.

Tosafot on Chullin 31a:15:1.hebrew: והא אמרה רבא חדא זימנא - אמתניתין לא פריך "הא תנינא חדא זימנא", כדפירש בקונטרס, משום דבמתניתין לא תנא בהדיא "הא הפילה הוא כשרה", אלא רבא הוא דדייק לה. ועוד, דאפילו אי תנן לה בהדיא במתניתין, לא היה יכול להקשות, דהא לא פריך ארבא "למה ליה למידק הא הפילה הוא כשרה, הא תנינא לעיל מדמכשרינן שחיטת חרש שוטה וקטן"; דאי לאו דאמר רבא אמתני' דחש"ו רבי נתן היא, לא היה מקשה כלום, דלמא בחש"ו מכשרינן טפי, ואפילו רבנן מודו דמיכווני לחתיכת בשר. אלא פריך משום דאוקמינן לההיא כרבי נתן, אלמא מכשרא מתניתין אפילו היכא דלא מיכוין לחתיכת בשר, כמו זרק סכין לנועצה בכותל; ואם כן, למה ליה לרבא למידק "הא הפילה הוא כשרה"? ומשני, דה"א לנועצה עדיף, דמיתכוין מיהא לחתיכה בעלמא, אבל הפילה לא מכוין כלל לשום חתיכה:
Tosafot on Chullin 31a:15:1.english: But Rava already said this once - [The Gemara] does not ask on the Mishnah, "But we already learned this once," as Rashi explained, because the Mishnah does not teach explicitly "but if he dropped it, it is valid"; rather, it is Rava who inferred it. Furthermore, even if we had learned it explicitly in the Mishnah, [the Gemara] could not have asked [this], for it does not ask on Rava, "Why did he need to infer 'but if he dropped it, it is valid'? We already learned it above, from the fact that we validate the slaughter of a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor!" For had Rava not said that the Mishnah about the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor follows Rabbi Natan, [the Gemara] would not have asked anything, since perhaps with a deaf-mute, imbecile and minor we validate more [leniently], and even the Rabbis would agree that they intend [to cut] a piece of flesh. Rather, it asks because we established that [Mishnah] as following Rabbi Natan; thus the Mishnah validates even where one did not intend to cut a piece of flesh, such as [where] he threw a knife in order to stick it into a wall. And if so, why did Rava need to infer "but if he dropped it, it is valid"? And [the Gemara] answers that one might have said [that the case of] sticking it [into the wall] is better, for he at least intended for some cutting in general, but [in the case of] dropping, he did not intend at all for any cutting.

Tosafot on Chullin 31a:16:1.hebrew: ואי אשמועינן הפילה - השתא הך צריכותא לא הויא דומיא דאידך, דלא בא לפרש טעם אמאי איצטריך ליה לרבא למימר גבי חרש שוטה וקטן רבי נתן היא, דא"כ מאי קאמר "אבל התם דלא אתי מכח בן דעת אימא לא"? הא בהדיא תנן דכשרה! אלא אמתניתין גופא עביד צריכותא אמאי איצטריך. ורבא איצטריך לאשמועינן דר' נתן היא, דאי לאו דאשמועינן הוה אמינא דהתם אפילו רבנן מודו, דהא מיכווני לחתיכת בשר; להכי אשמועינן דאפ"ה פסלי רבנן. והא דקאמר רבא לקמן "ורבנן נהי דלא בעי כוונה לזביחה, לחתיכה מיהא בעיא", היינו לחתיכת סימנים:
Tosafot on Chullin 31a:16:1.english: And if it had taught us [the case of] "he made it fall" - Now, this [explanation of the] need [for both cases] is not similar to the other, for [Tosafot] does not come to explain the reason why Rava needed to say, regarding a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, that it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Natan. For if so, what is [the Gemara] saying: "But there, where it does not come from the power of a person with intent, I might say no"? Surely we learned explicitly that it is valid! Rather, [Tosafot] is constructing the need [for both cases] on the Mishnah itself, [to explain] why it was needed. And Rava needed to teach us that it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Natan, for had he not taught us, I would have said that there, even the Rabbis agree, since he does direct his intent toward cutting a piece of flesh; therefore he teaches us that nevertheless the Rabbis invalidate. And as for what Rava says below, "And the Rabbis: granted that they do not require intent for slaughtering, for cutting they do require [it]," this refers to cutting the simanim (the windpipe and gullet).

Tosafot on Chullin 31a:18:1.hebrew: ואסורה לאכול בתרומה - אפילו למעשר אסורה, כדאמרי' בסמוך; אלא נקט תרומה, דנוהגת בזמן הזה:
Tosafot on Chullin 31a:18:1.english: And she is forbidden to eat terumah - She is forbidden even [to eat] ma'aser, as we say shortly below; but [the Gemara] mentioned terumah because it applies nowadays:

Tosafot on Chullin 31a:19:1.hebrew: עון כרת התרת - איפכא הוה ליה למימר: עון מיתה אסרת, עון כרת מיבעיא! דהא פשיטא דבעינן כוונה בתרומה, וכדתנן בחומר בקדש (חגיגה דף יח:): טבל לחולין, אסור במעשר. ואף בחולין בעי רבא למימר דטבל ולא הוחזק כאילו לא טבל. ויש לומר משום דנקט מעיקרא "טהורה לביתה", קאמר הכי. אי נמי, נאנסה עדיף מטבל לחולין, שאם היתה יודעת היתה מתכוונת אף למעשר. ומדקאמר "טהורה לביתה", אלמא חשיבא ליה כוונה, אם כן אף לתרומה תהא מותרת:
Tosafot on Chullin 31a:19:1.english: You permitted a transgression [punishable by] karet - He should have said the reverse: "You forbade a transgression [punishable by] death, [and] all the more so a transgression [punishable by] karet!" For it is obvious that intention is required for terumah, as we learned in [the chapter on] the stringency of sacred things (Chagigah 18b): One who immersed for the sake of ordinary food is forbidden [to partake of] ma'aser. And even regarding ordinary food, Rava wished to say that one who immersed is not considered as though [she] had not immersed. And one can say that because [Rava] began with "pure for her husband's house," he said it this way. Alternatively, [a woman] who was compelled is better off than one who immersed for the sake of ordinary food, since if she had known, she would have had intention even for ma'aser. And since he said "pure for her husband's house," evidently he considers intention significant; if so, she should be permitted even for terumah.

Tosafot on Chullin 31a:5:1.hebrew: חוץ לצואר כמלא צואר - לכאורה נראה שצריך להוליך כל אותו מלא צואר שחוץ לצואר, ולכך צריך אותו שיעור. ומיהו נראה דאין צריך, ולא הוצרך שיעור זה אלא כדי שישחוט בריוח; ופעמים שהסכין חריף, ושוחט הרוב בלא הולכת כמלא צואר:
Tosafot on Chullin 31a:5:1.english: Outside the neck, the width of a neck - At first glance it appears that one must carry [the knife] that entire neck's-width that is outside the neck, and this is why that measure is required. However, it appears that this is not required, and this measure was needed only so that one may slaughter comfortably; and sometimes the knife is sharp, and one slaughters the majority [of the windpipe] without carrying [the knife] the width of a neck.
